data.body: DESIGN DECISION (operator-ratified, grounded in OSS research): adopt option (b) — the richer probe contract — NOT option (a) silent skip-when-empty. The probe port must distinguish unavailable/could-not-check from checked-and-failed from checked-and-clean, and doctor output must render 'could not check' distinctly rather than dropping the link axis or reporting false drift errors. Precedent: (1) Flutter doctor's ValidationType enum has a distinct notAvailable state rendered '[!] Could not check X' — it never masquerades as ✗ (failure) or ✓ (clean); (2) Homebrew's diagnostic checks are typed T.nilable(Finding), where nil = 'could not evaluate' is a different type from a Finding. rebar equivalent: make issue_link_types() failure observable (e.g. return None / raise-and-catch at the probe seam instead of fail-soft []), and fold a link-types probe failure into the 'unavailable' finding for that axis so a partial probe failure (link-types API errors while statuses/types succeed) degrades to 'could not check links' instead of producing a blocking drift ERROR for every configured link target.
